liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bird Song** (2 reviews): Reviewer considers this possibly the best early-80s Bird Song they saw; says it sparkles when played loud; Jerry and Bob get a nice mix going into the jam, playing nearly clean guitars in the big hall [23][26]
- **Alabama Getaway** (1 review): The show opens solidly with Alabama Getaway into Greatest Story Ever Told [26]
- **Loser** (1 review): Loser is one of the reviewer's favorites from that night [31]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): China Cat into Rider is a highlight, along with the post-drums sequence [32]
- **To Lay Me Down** (1 review): To Lay Me Down seems to ignite the rest of the second set [32]
- **(I Can't Get No) Satisfaction** (1 review): Satisfaction is another of the reviewer's favorite moments from that night [31]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-04-09.sbd.miller.107054.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 147 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd1982-04-09.sbd.miller.32716.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 149 min; rated 3.88/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: Soundboard remaster by Miller is described as clean and clear [29]
- **gd1982-04-09.169767.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 152 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd82-04-09.fobsenn441-eaton.sacks.28204.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 151 min; rated 3.86/5 by 7 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the audience recording's sound too hollow, though calls the show solid and rocking [21]
- **gd1982-04-09.155211.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 147 min [8]
- **gd1982-04-09.179594.Renninger.mattes.carbonetta.visser.flac2496**: source not stated; 21 songs; 146 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [11]

## Around the show

- Reviewer stood on the general admission floor in the first set; crowd was loose and danced, with balloons and upstate herbs around [24]
- Reviewer recalls the hockey-rink-like venue, a friendly Rochester crowd, and Genesee beer [31]
- Reviewer calls this the last great Jerry period, when he felt each note and attended to the band [24]
- Reviewer says the clean, minimally processed guitar interplay was something the band lost completely in later years [26]
- Reviewer hears the band carving out a new sound with Brent, whose grainy voice and frenzied organ energize it [32]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-04-09.sbd.miller.107054.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat (48k) [1]. Also: This soundboard is a remaster of shnid 32716, with pitch correction help from Joe B. Jones [1]
- **gd1982-04-09.sbd.miller.32716.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat (48k) [2]
- **gd1982-04-09.169767.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Bob Wagner's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell XLII-S90) [3]. Also: A Sennheiser 421 source from Jim Vita supplies a 2:23 patch in Drums [3]
- **gd82-04-09.fobsenn441-eaton.sacks.28204.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Rob Eaton; source: Audience Recording: Sennheiser 441's [6]
- **gd1982-04-09.155211.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell XLIIS 90) [8]
- **gd1982-04-09.179594.Renninger.mattes.carbonetta.visser.flac2496**: taped by Kenn Renninger; transferred by Nick Carbonetta; source: Master - Shure SM57 > Marantz Superscope [11]. Also: Cassettes come from the collection of taper and trader Kenn Renninger, shared through his wife Peg [11]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1982-04-09 Community War Memorial Auditorium, Rochester, NY, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1982-04-09-community-war-memorial-auditorium-rochester-ny-usa/) [34]
